log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 49% BRING: garchomp, 21% BRING: rotom, 16% BRING: blaziken
Pick 2: 45% BRING: rotom, 21% BRING: sceptile, 19% BRING: blaziken
Pick 3: 47% BRING: blaziken, 29% BRING: taurospaldeablaze, 17% BRING: delphox

Plan: Lead Incineroar to use Intimidate and Fake Out. Garchomp (Mega) is the main sweeper and Gholdengo covers special attacks. Opponent has many Fire types and Rotom (Levitate, so Earthquake won't hit it). Expect Fire and Fighting attacks, so keep Incineroar's Parting Shot for scouting or chip damage. Watch Blaziken and Delphox speed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick a team of 3 against this fire-heavy opponent lineup with Rotom, Tauros, Delphox, Blaziken, Sceptile, and Garchomp. Kingambit seems solid against the Psychic and Fire threats, while Corviknight could struggle against fire moves, so I'm weighing Gholdengo and Incineroar as other options.

Settling on Incineroar as lead for intimidate and fake out support, Garchomp for mega evolution power, and Gholdengo for coverage.

decisions.thought: 50% SWITCH: blaziken, 30% SWITCH: rotom, 11% MOVE: stoneedge

Opponent lead Garchomp (Atk -1 from my Intimidate). It outspeeds Incineroar, so Fake Out (flinch, first-turn only) is the best opener. Possible Mega Garchomp threat: keep Gholdengo for special damage and Garchomp (mine, Mega) for sweeping later. Opponent threats: Blaziken, Delphox, Taurospaldea (Fire/Fighting), Sceptile, Rotom (Levitate, so no Earthquake on it). Save Parting Shot for scouting/switching.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: It's turn 1 against Garchomp, already at -1 Attack from intimidate. Fake Out seems like a strong opening move here since it's neutral damage and would flinch Garchomp before it can act, even though it outspeeds us normally—though I should consider the possibility they're running Mega Garchomp.

decisions.thought: 63% MOVE: blastburn [MEGA], 26% MOVE: blastburn, 2% MOVE: reversal [MEGA]

Opponent: Blaziken (Fire/Fighting, Speed Boost or Blaze) is active at 80%. Garchomp was their lead and is benched, with its Atk lowered by my Intimidate. Rotom, Taurospaldea, Delphox and Sceptile are unscouted. Fighting moves are dangerous to Incineroar, while Gholdengo is immune to Fighting and resists Fire. Plan: bring Gholdengo in now, use Shadow Ball or Make It Rain on Blaziken, and keep Garchomp for a later sweep. Expect a Garchomp switch-in later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is active against Blaziken at 80%, while Garchomp, the opposing lead, got hit with Intimidate before switching out and is now benched with lowered Attack. I'm weighing Flare Blitz on Blaziken as the next move.

Flare Blitz isn't great here since Fire is resisted by Fire. Parting Shot could lower Blaziken's Atk/SpA and pivot me to Garchomp or Gholdengo, but Blaziken likely outspeeds and could hit Incineroar hard with Close Combat since Fighting is super effective against Dark. Switching to Gholdengo looks promising since its Steel/Ghost typing makes it immune to Fighting-type moves entirely.

Actually switching directly to Gholdengo seems safer: it resists or is immune to whatever Blaziken throws, keeps Incineroar safe from a hit, though it sacrifices the scouting benefit Parting Shot would've given.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo fainted to Mega Blaziken's Blast Burn. Blaziken is Fire/Fighting, so Garchomp (Dragon/Ground) resists Fire and Earthquake hits it super effectively. Incineroar is weak to Fighting. Switching in Garchomp. Next turn, consider Mega Garchomp and Earthquake on Blaziken if Garchomp is faster. Opponent still has Rotom, Taurospaldea, Delphox or Sceptile to come, and Garchomp's Atk was lowered by my Intimidate.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Gholdengo down, I need to switch to either Garchomp or Incineroar against their Speed-boosted Mega Blaziken, weighing how Fire/Fighting coverage interacts with Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing.

Incineroar's Dark typing is weak to Fighting, making it risky, while Garchomp resists Fire and can hit back with a super effective Earthquake. I'll switch to Garchomp as the safer, more offensive option, with mega evolution available on a later turn.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Mega Blaziken (Speed Boost, now +1) probably outspeeds my Garchomp, so I can't rely on moving first. Blast Burn is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing. Earthquake is 2x on Blaziken's Fire typing. I'm Mega-evolving Garchomp now and using Earthquake to knock Blaziken out. Opponent still has Garchomp (100%, unseen moves), Rotom, Taurospaldea, Delphox and Sceptile to come. Keep Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot for later switches.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm tracking the battle state: my non-mega Garchomp at 169 speed against the opposing Mega Blaziken with speed boost, now at 80% health, while trying to recall whether the opposing Garchomp still on field is the same one that led and got hit by Intimidate.

Typing-wise, Blaziken's Fire/Fighting attacks are only neutral-to-resisted against my Dragon/Ground Garchomp, while my Earthquake hits Blaziken for 2x since it's part Fire. I'm estimating that Earthquake from my Mega Garchomp, with its boosted attack stat, should do heavy damage to Blaziken's remaining ~150 HP, likely close to a KO.

But speed matters here: with its +1 boost, Blaziken now outspeeds my Garchomp significantly, so it moves first. Since Blast Burn is resisted, it would more likely switch to Close Combat for neutral damage instead. I'm weighing whether to Mega Evolve my Garchomp now to get Earthquake in, accepting that Blaziken strikes first with Close Combat before I can retaliate.

decisions.thought: 70% SWITCH: garchomp, 12% MOVE: poltergeist, 10% MOVE: voltswitch

Mega Garchomp is faster than Rotom and immune to its Electric moves. Earthquake won't hit Rotom because of Levitate, so don't use it there. Swords Dance now is safe: Rotom's likely attacks do little to Garchomp. Opponent still has an unseen Garchomp, which could come in and threaten my Garchomp. Incineroar (Intimidate, Parting Shot) and Stone Edge are available if needed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Mega Garchomp is at full HP facing the opponent's Rotom, which has levitate making it immune to Ground-type moves like Earthquake despite its Electric/Ghost typing. The opponent's team also includes a Garchomp and Blaziken still in reserve, so I need to factor that into my move choice here.

Stone Edge or Dragon Claw would be neutral hits on Rotom, but since Garchomp is immune to Electric and has no Ghost weakness, Rotom can't really punish me much. That makes Swords Dance a relatively safe setup option right now, boosting my attack before switching to Stone Edge or Dragon Claw, though I should watch out for the opponent's Garchomp coming in with its own Earthquake.

decisions.thought: 87% SWITCH: rotom, 7% MOVE: stoneedge, 4% MOVE: sandstorm

Turn 5: My Mega Garchomp (Atk +2, faster than most Garchomp) faces their unseen Garchomp (Sand Veil or Rough Skin). Dragon Claw is super effective on it, so I'm attacking with that. Opponent still has Rotom (Levitate, Electric/Ghost) and possibly Taurospaldea, Delphox, or Sceptile to come. Keep Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot for later switches. Avoid Earthquake on Rotom.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Opponent's Garchomp is at full health, and my Mega Garchomp has boosted attack with a speed edge. Dragon Claw would hit super effectively against it, and Earthquake is another strong option to consider.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: 35% MOVE: spikes, 27% MOVE: stoneedge, 21% MOVE: stealthrock

Mega Garchomp is at full HP with Atk +2 and is likely faster than their Garchomp. Their Blaziken, Rotom and the Gholdengo are down. Dragon Claw is 2x on their Garchomp, so keep attacking with it. Remaining opponent threats are Taurospaldea, Delphox and Sceptile. Save Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot for switching in against a bad matchup. Avoid Earthquake on Rotom (Levitate).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Mega Garchomp is at full HP with Attack boosted twice, facing an opposing Garchomp at full health with an unknown item. I'm checking the type matchup—Dragon Claw against a Dragon/Ground target should hit for double damage from the Dragon typing while the Ground typing is neutral against it.

Earthquake would be resisted since Garchomp itself is Ground-type, and Stone Edge isn't very effective either, so Dragon Claw is clearly the best option here. The opposing Garchomp's ability and speed are uncertain, but sticking with Dragon Claw is the right call regardless.
